question: The Intercept recently reported that the European Leadership Network (ELNET), a pro-Israel lobbying group based in the EU, has received donations of more than USD 11 million from donors based in the United States since 2022.1 The purpose of this organisation is specifically to advocate on behalf of a non-EU country and it is in receipt of a substantial amount of funding from a separate third country.

It is deeply troubling that an organisation that receives substantial funding from non-EU donors could have significant access to EU policymakers, as it claims on its website. Can the Commission confirm: 1.
The number of occasions on which its (including European External Action Service) staff have met with individuals from ELNET since June 2024?
Whether they were aware of the significant amount of donations from the United States which this organisation receives?
Whether they will refuse to meet with individuals from ELNET in the future given that they are being funded by one non-EU country to lobby directly in the interests of another non-EU country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.2.2026) The Commission is engaging with the European Leadership Network (ELNET) as it does with many non-governmental organisations which receive funding from different sources.

Among other activities ELNET organises visits for former high-level Israeli officials and opinion makers to visit the European Institutions and requests meetings with senior EU officials at their events. Schedule permitting, the European External Action Service (EEAS) senior management may meet these delegations at appropriate level for usual exchanges of information.

Commission and EEAS officials are regularly invited to speak at ELNET events, organised in Brussels or in Tel Aviv, on major geopolitical issues in the Middle East, to an audience of governmental and non-governmental participants. These events present opportunities for the EU to publicly express the EU’s position regarding the Middle East.

Pursuant to the Interinstitutional Agreement on the transparency register1, legal entities, offices or networks without diplomatic status or intermediaries representing public authorities of third countries are eligible to register in the transparency register. ELNET is registered2 and is required to provide in its registration the financial information set out in Annex II to the Interinstitutional Agreement.

The Commission publishes its meetings held with ELNET in an interest representation context in accordance with the applicable Commission’s transparency rules. A list of such meetings is available on ELNET’s registration in the Transparency Register.
